newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA's 1996 results show slow recovery.
newsitem.headline: ICA's 1996 results show slow recovery.

text.p: ICA SA's 1996 results show the Mexican building products company is slowly pulling out of its post-devaluation slump.
ICA reported 1996 earnings of 4.61 pesos per share after dilution, exceeding an average forecast of 3.86 pesos by six industry analysts surveyed by Reuters.
Analysts said the difference largely reflected higher-than-expected accounting gains, although the company's operating results were positive.
"The market was aware that (the results) were not going to be fantastic, however they came out higher than market expectations" said Ben Uglow, a cement industry analyst at Robert Flemings.
Uglow said the company's fourth-quarter sales of 1.994 billion were four percent higher than his estimate, and its operating profits of 126 million pesos exceeded his forecast by about seven percent.

"We are starting to see a recovery in the number of projects in a steady, sustained way. ICA is beginning to merit the premium on its shares," said Gerardo Saenz, an analyst at OBSA-Serfin in Mexico City.
ICA's share price has shown little change since the middle of last year. On Tuesday, it dipped 1.80 to 129.20, compared with its 52-week high of 138.80. The stock's year-low is 85.60.

Alvaro Shiraishe, an analyst at UBS Securities in New York, said ICA's share price may have languished in recent months because some investors thought it was taking too long to recover from the crisis.
He said investors may have unfairly compared 1996 results with those in 1995, when the company still had some projects carried over from before the 1994 peso devaluation.
